title: Container killed for exceeding its memory limit
cause: The container used more memory than its limit allows, so the kernel killed it (exit code 137).

fixes.title: Check the current memory limit and actual usage
fixes.command: kubectl describe pod -l app={deployment} -n {namespace} | grep -A3 -i limits && kubectl top pod -l app={deployment} -n {namespace}
fixes.verify: Compare the limit with the usage shown by kubectl top.

fixes.title: Raise the memory limit for the deployment
fixes.verify: kubectl rollout status deployment/{deployment} -n {namespace}

fixes.title: For Node.js, cap the heap below the container limit
fixes.verify: kubectl get pods -l app={deployment} -n {namespace} -w  (pods stay Running, restart count stops increasing)

prevention: Set memory requests and limits from measured usage plus headroom, and alert on usage above 80 percent of the limit.

title: Image or tag does not exist in the registry
cause: The deployment references an image name or tag that the registry cannot find, usually a typo or a tag that was never pushed.

fixes.title: Confirm which image the pod is trying to pull
fixes.verify: The printed image and tag should match what CI pushed.

fixes.title: Check that the tag exists in the registry
fixes.verify: The command prints a manifest instead of 'no such manifest'.

fixes.title: Point the deployment at a tag that exists in the registry
fixes.verify: kubectl rollout status deployment/{deployment} -n {namespace}

prevention: Deploy by immutable digest or the exact tag produced by the CI run, never a hand-typed tag.

title: Kubernetes cannot pull the container image
cause: Kubernetes keeps failing to pull the image and is backing off. This is a symptom; the line before it says whether the tag is missing or the registry rejected the credentials.

fixes.title: Read the exact pull error for the pod
fixes.command: kubectl describe pod -l app={deployment} -n {namespace} | grep -A3 -i 'failed to pull'
fixes.verify: The message says not found (wrong tag) or unauthorized (credentials).

prevention: Deploy by the exact image digest CI produced, from a registry the cluster has credentials for.

title: Registry rejected the credentials
patterns: denied: requested access to the resource is denied
cause: The cluster or build runner has no valid credentials for a private registry, or the token has expired.

fixes.title: Check which pull secret the pod uses
fixes.verify: A secret name is listed and exists: kubectl get secret <name> -n {namespace}

fixes.title: Recreate the registry pull secret
fixes.verify: kubectl get secret regcred -n {namespace}

fixes.title: Attach the secret to the deployment
fixes.verify: kubectl rollout status deployment/{deployment} -n {namespace}

prevention: Use a robot or service account token for the registry and track its expiry date.

title: npm could not resolve dependency versions
patterns: ERESOLVE unable to resolve dependency tree
cause: Two packages require incompatible versions of a shared dependency, so npm install stops during the build.

fixes.title: Reproduce the conflict locally to see which packages clash
fixes.verify: The output names the conflicting package versions.

fixes.title: Use the lockfile in CI instead of resolving fresh
fixes.verify: npm ci exits with code 0.

fixes.title: Align the conflicting versions in package.json, then regenerate the lockfile
fixes.verify: docker build . completes without npm ERR! lines.

prevention: Commit package-lock.json and run npm ci in the Dockerfile.

title: Native Node module failed to compile
cause: A package with native code has no prebuilt binary for this Node version or base image and the image lacks build tools, often after a Node version change.

fixes.title: Check which Node version the base image uses
fixes.verify: Compare with the version used by the last successful build.

fixes.title: Pin the base image to the Node version that last worked
fixes.verify: docker build . completes without gyp ERR! lines.

fixes.title: Or upgrade the native package to a version with prebuilt binaries
fixes.verify: npm ls {package} shows the new version and the build passes.

prevention: Pin the base image tag (node:18.20-bullseye rather than node:latest).

title: pip could not find a matching package version
patterns: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement (?P<package>\S+)
cause: A pinned Python package version does not exist for this Python version or platform, or the version constraints conflict.

fixes.title: List the versions available for this Python version
fixes.verify: The pinned version appears in the list.

fixes.title: Check the Python version in the image
fixes.verify: The package supports this Python version.

fixes.title: Update the pin in requirements.txt and rebuild
fixes.verify: The dry run resolves without errors.

prevention: Generate pins with pip-compile against the same Python version as the image.

title: Dockerfile COPY source file is missing
patterns: COPY failed: (?:file not found|stat|no source files).*?(?P<path>[\w./-]+)?
failed to compute cache key: .*"?(?P<path>/[\w./-]+)"?: not found
failed to calculate checksum of ref .*"(?P<path>[^"]+)": not found
cause: A file referenced by COPY or ADD is not in the build context, usually because of .dockerignore or a wrong relative path.

fixes.title: Confirm the file exists relative to the build context
fixes.verify: The file is listed.

fixes.title: Check whether .dockerignore excludes it
fixes.verify: No pattern matches the missing path.

fixes.title: Fix the COPY path in the Dockerfile and rebuild
fixes.verify: The build passes the COPY step.

prevention: Run docker build in CI on every pull request, not only on deploy.

title: Port is already in use
cause: Another process or container is already listening on the port the application tries to bind.

fixes.title: Find what is listening on the port
fixes.verify: The output shows the conflicting process or container.

fixes.title: List containers publishing the port
fixes.verify: An old container holding the port appears in the list.

fixes.title: Stop the old container
fixes.verify: lsof -i :{port} returns nothing, then restart the new container.

prevention: Stop the previous release before starting the new one, or let the orchestrator manage ports.

title: Disk is full on the build or node host
cause: The host has no free disk space, usually from accumulated images, build cache or logs.

fixes.title: Check disk usage on the host
fixes.verify: Identify which filesystem is full.

fixes.title: Remove dangling build cache only
fixes.verify: docker system df shows reclaimed space.

prevention: Schedule build cache cleanup on runners and alert on disk above 85 percent.

title: Build or container command exited with an error
patterns: did not complete successfully: exit code: (?P<code>\d+)
cause: A command in the build or container stopped with a non-zero exit code. The real reason is in the lines just before this one.

fixes.title: Show the full output of the failing step
fixes.verify: The first error above the exit code names the real cause.

prevention: Fail fast in scripts with set -euo pipefail so the first error is the one reported.

title: Pod is restarting in a crash loop
cause: The container starts and exits repeatedly. This is a symptom; the cause is in the container's own logs before it exits.

fixes.title: Read the logs of the previous crashed container
fixes.verify: The last lines before exit show the real error.

fixes.title: Check the exit reason and code
fixes.command: kubectl describe pod -l app={deployment} -n {namespace} | grep -A5 'Last State'
fixes.verify: Reason shows OOMKilled, Error, or Completed with an exit code.

prevention: Make startup errors log clearly before the process exits.

title: Health check probe failing
cause: The app is not answering its health endpoint in time. Either the app is failing to start, or the probe path, port or timing is wrong.

fixes.title: Check the probe configuration
fixes.verify: Path and port match what the app actually serves.

fixes.title: Call the health endpoint from inside the pod
fixes.verify: The endpoint returns 200.

fixes.title: Give slow-starting apps more time
fixes.verify: kubectl rollout status deployment/{deployment} -n {namespace}

prevention: Use a startup probe for apps with slow initialization.

title: Load balancer has no healthy backend
patterns: connect\(\) failed .* while connecting to upstream
cause: Traffic reaches the load balancer but no backend pod is ready to serve it. This is a downstream symptom of the app failing.

fixes.title: Check whether the service has ready endpoints
fixes.verify: At least one pod IP is listed.

prevention: Use rolling updates with maxUnavailable 0 so old pods keep serving until new ones are ready.

title: Required environment variable is missing
cause: The application needs an environment variable that the deployment does not provide, often a secret or config value missing in this environment.

fixes.title: List the environment variables the deployment sets
fixes.verify: If nothing prints, the variable is missing.

fixes.title: Check whether the referenced secret or config map has the key
fixes.verify: Find the object that should contain {env_var}.

fixes.title: Add the variable from a secret
fixes.verify: kubectl rollout status deployment/{deployment} -n {namespace}

prevention: Validate required configuration at startup and keep a checked-in .env.example listing every key.

title: Configuration file could not be parsed
cause: A YAML or JSON configuration file has a syntax error, often an indentation mistake or unquoted special character.

fixes.title: Validate Kubernetes manifests without applying them
fixes.verify: The command reports no parse errors.

fixes.title: Lint the YAML file
fixes.verify: No errors are reported at the reported line.

prevention: Run yamllint and kubectl --dry-run in CI before deploy.

title: Permission denied on a file or socket
cause: The process runs as a user that lacks access to a file, directory, port or API resource.

fixes.title: Check which user the container runs as and the file owner
fixes.verify: The user owns or can read the path.

fixes.title: For Kubernetes RBAC errors, check what the service account may do
fixes.verify: The required verb and resource are listed.

prevention: Set file ownership in the Dockerfile with COPY --chown and run as a fixed non-root UID.

title: TLS certificate is invalid or expired
patterns: unable to verify the first certificate
cause: A TLS connection failed certificate verification because the certificate is expired, self-signed, or for a different hostname.

fixes.title: Inspect the certificate the server presents
fixes.verify: notAfter is in the future and the subject matches the host.

prevention: Automate renewal with cert-manager and alert 14 days before expiry.

title: No node has enough resources to schedule the pod
cause: The pod's resource requests are larger than the free capacity on every node, so it stays Pending.

fixes.title: See free capacity per node
fixes.verify: Compare free capacity with the pod requests.

fixes.title: Lower the requests if they are oversized
fixes.verify: kubectl get pods -n {namespace} shows the pod moving out of Pending.

prevention: Set requests from measured usage and enable the cluster autoscaler.

title: Hostname could not be resolved
cause: The application tries to reach a hostname that DNS cannot resolve, usually a wrong service name or a missing service in this namespace.

fixes.title: Resolve the name from inside the cluster
fixes.verify: The name resolves to an address.

fixes.title: List services in the namespace to find the correct name
fixes.verify: The intended service exists under the name the app uses.

prevention: Use the fully qualified service name (service.namespace.svc.cluster.local) in configuration.

title: Test suite failed in the pipeline
cause: One or more automated tests failed, so the pipeline stopped before deploying.

fixes.title: Run the failing test locally
fixes.verify: The test fails locally with the same assertion, then passes after the fix.

prevention: Run tests on pull requests so failures are caught before merge.

title: Database refused the connection
patterns: could not connect to server: Connection refused
cause: Nothing is accepting connections at the database host and port the app uses: the database is down, not yet ready, or the host or port in the configuration is wrong.

fixes.title: Check that the database pod or service is running
fixes.verify: The database pod is Running and the service exists.

fixes.title: Test the port from the app's network
fixes.verify: nc reports the port open.

fixes.title: Check the host and port the app is configured with
fixes.verify: The values match the database service name and port.

prevention: Add an init container or retry with backoff so the app waits for the database instead of crashing.

title: Database rejected the username or password
cause: The database credentials the app uses do not match a valid user, often because a secret was rotated or differs between environments.

fixes.title: Check which secret supplies the database password
fixes.command: kubectl get deployment {deployment} -n {namespace} -o yaml | grep -B2 -A4 -i secretKeyRef
fixes.verify: Note the secret name and key.

fixes.title: Test the credentials directly
fixes.verify: The query returns 1.

fixes.title: Restart the app after updating the secret so it reads the new value
fixes.verify: kubectl rollout status deployment/{deployment} -n {namespace}

prevention: Store credentials in one secret manager and sync to the cluster instead of editing secrets by hand.

title: Database name does not exist
cause: The app connects to a database name that has not been created on this server.

fixes.title: List the databases on the server
fixes.verify: Check whether {db_name} is listed.

fixes.title: Create the database
fixes.verify: psql -h {host} -U {user} -d {db_name} -c 'select 1' returns 1.

prevention: Create databases through migrations or infrastructure code, not by hand.

title: Schema migration has not been applied
cause: The new code expects a table or column that does not exist yet, because the database migration did not run before the app started.

fixes.title: Check migration status
fixes.command: kubectl exec deploy/{deployment} -n {namespace} -- npx prisma migrate status
fixes.verify: The output lists the unapplied migration. Use your tool's equivalent: alembic current, rails db:migrate:status.

fixes.title: Apply pending migrations
fixes.command: kubectl exec deploy/{deployment} -n {namespace} -- npx prisma migrate deploy
fixes.verify: Migration status reports the database is up to date.

prevention: Run migrations as a pre-deploy job or init container so the app never starts against an old schema.

title: Database connection timed out
patterns: Connection is not available, request timed out
cause: The app can reach the network path but gets no answer in time, often a firewall or security group blocking the port, or a database under heavy load.

fixes.title: Test reachability from the app's network
fixes.verify: nc connects within 5 seconds.

fixes.title: Check network policies in the namespace
fixes.verify: No policy blocks egress from the app to the database port.

prevention: Document required ports in the network policy alongside the deployment.

title: Database connection limit reached
cause: Every replica opens its own pool, and together they exceed the database max_connections, often after scaling up.

fixes.title: Check the server limit and current usage
fixes.verify: Usage is close to the limit.

fixes.title: Reduce the pool size per replica
fixes.verify: pg_stat_activity count drops below the limit.

prevention: Size pools as max_connections divided by replica count, or use a pooler such as PgBouncer.

title: Database requires an encrypted connection
patterns: no pg_hba\.conf entry for host .* (?:SSL off|no encryption)
cause: The database only accepts TLS connections but the app connects without SSL, or the reverse.

fixes.title: Enable SSL in the connection string
fixes.verify: kubectl logs deployment/{deployment} -n {namespace} shows a successful connection.

prevention: Keep sslmode explicit in every environment's connection string.
